title: Bad junta node batch
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $P$ be a set of coordinates, and let $z$ assign signs to the coordinates in $P$. Fix a natural number $k$, a failure parameter in $(0,1/2]$, and a batch of the specified restricted-sample size, each sample consisting of an assignment on the coordinates outside $P$ together with a sign. The batch is bad exactly when the node decision computed from it is not correct for the restriction of $f$ obtained by fixing $P$ according to $z$.
